beats.label: S1 · The blackmail
beats.text: Jesse is blackmailed with a lewd party tape; he, Judy, and Kelvin secretly gather cash to pay it off, hiding the crisis from their father Eli.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets in motion the season's core plot and the sibling conspiracy against Eli.

beats.label: S1 · The drop turns deadly
beats.text: The parking-lot handoff collapses into violence: the siblings run one masked blackmailer over as they flee, and Jesse deliberately reverses over another.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns the siblings into killers and gives the surviving blackmailers a personal grudge.

beats.label: S1 · The third man is Gideon
beats.text: The third masked accomplice slips onto the compound and is revealed as Jesse's estranged son Gideon, back from a failed L.A. stunt career.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts the season's ticking bomb inside the family and drives the Jesse-Gideon reconciliation arc.

beats.label: S1 · Baby Billy returns
beats.text: Aimee-Leigh's brother Baby Billy comes back to run a mall church, reopening old wounds about the late matriarch but slotting back into the family.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reinstalls Baby Billy as a permanent Gemstone fixture for every season that follows.

beats.label: S1 · Vault robbery
beats.text: Surviving blackmailer Scotty robs the church vault. He is hit by Baby Billy's car; Tiffany shoots him dead, and Billy quietly pockets the cash.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Billy's larceny, Tiffany's steel, and the missing money that snaps the family open.

beats.label: S1 · The truth breaks the family
beats.text: Gideon takes the fall for the robbery to protect his father and leaves in disgrace. Amber discovers the sex tape and shoots Jesse in the buttocks.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Blows up Jesse's marriage and Gideon's place in the family, setting the S2 opening reset.

beats.label: S1 · Confession and exile
beats.text: The kids confess everything to Eli, who fires them. Billy, struck by lightning, returns the cash; Jesse flies to Haiti to reunite with Gideon.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Delivers the end-of-season status quo the next season inherits.

cliffhanger.text: Jesse has fled to Haiti to win back Gideon after Amber threw him out, and the three siblings have been fired from the ministry with everything to prove to their father.
questions: Can Jesse repair his marriage and bring Gideon home?
Will Eli let his children back into the church he just took from them?
What does Baby Billy do with his new fame as the preacher who came back from the dead?

characters.name: Eli Gemstone
characters.line: Widowed patriarch of the family megachurch, who has just fired his three children after learning what they hid from him.

characters.name: Jesse Gemstone
characters.line: Eldest son, thrown out by his wife Amber over the sex tape, now in Haiti trying to reconnect with his estranged son Gideon.

characters.name: Judy Gemstone
characters.line: Only Gemstone daughter, reconciled at last with her fiancé BJ, still starved for Eli's respect and a real ministry role.

characters.name: Kelvin Gemstone
characters.line: Youngest son, has just rescued his friend Keefe from a satanic cult and brought him home to the compound.

characters.name: Baby Billy Freeman
characters.line: Aimee-Leigh's opportunistic brother, now a tent-revival evangelist trading on his lightning strike and 'heaven vision'.

characters.name: Gideon Gemstone
characters.line: Jesse's estranged son, took the fall for the church robbery and has left for Haiti as a missionary.

characters.name: Amber Gemstone
characters.line: Jesse's wife, discovered his infidelity via the sex tape and threw him out of the house.

characters.name: Tiffany Freeman
characters.line: Baby Billy's much younger wife, killed the blackmailer Scotty in a panic and returned the stolen money with her husband.

characters.name: BJ
characters.line: Judy's soft-spoken fiancé, just reconciled with her after she publicly humiliated him.

characters.name: Keefe Chambers
characters.line: Kelvin's rescued former-satanist companion, now living with him on the compound.

beats.label: S2 · Zion's Landing
beats.text: Jesse partners with Texan televangelists Lyle and Lindy Lissons on a Christian resort, Zion's Landing; Eli reluctantly gives his blessing.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Lissons and their resort are the season's engine and end up defining its casualties.

beats.label: S2 · The reporter's body
beats.text: Investigative reporter Thaniel Block is found dead at his cabin, and the siblings arrive to find Eli already there with blood on his shirt.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants the season-long suspicion that Eli may be a murderer, and the mystery of who really killed Block.

beats.label: S2 · Junior returns
beats.text: Eli's old wrestling friend Junior, son of a mobster who once threatened the family, reappears; when Eli tries to break it off, Junior declares them enemies.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's ambiguous menace and the hidden history that shadows Eli.

beats.label: S2 · Thumbs and the Cycle Ninjas
beats.text: At BJ's baptism party, Kelvin provokes Eli, who breaks his thumbs. Hours later, masked assassins on motorbikes ambush Jesse and Amber at a gas station.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Fractures the family internally just as an external threat opens fire on them.

beats.label: S2 · Roy's secret
beats.text: A 1993 flashback shows Eli's senile father Roy killed mobster Glendon Marsh Sr. after threats to the family; Eli hid the body and never told Junior.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains Junior's grievance and the guilt Eli carries into the season's endgame.

beats.label: S2 · Coma and counter-trap
beats.text: The Cycle Ninjas shoot Eli, putting him in a coma. His kids fake his recovery to bait them; Gideon runs the assassins off the road as Eli finally wakes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Forces the siblings to fight for their father and pulls them back into a functioning unit.

beats.label: S2 · Lissons exposed
beats.text: Junior forgives Eli and reveals the Ninjas were teens from Lyle Lisson's orphanage. The Gemstones seize Zion's Landing; Martin has the Ninjas kill the Lissons.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the season's antagonists and hands the family a huge new asset heading into S3.

cliffhanger.text: With the Lissons dead and Zion's Landing seized, the Gemstones look victorious, but Eli has been quietly stepping back and the question of who actually runs the church is still open.
questions: Which sibling will really take over the ministry?
Can Jesse, Judy, and Kelvin lead as equals, or will their egos split them?
Now that Eli has stopped being the shield between his kids and the outside world, who will come for them next?

characters.name: Eli Gemstone
characters.line: Recovered from the assassination attempt, quietly starting to hand the church over to his children.

characters.name: Jesse Gemstone
characters.line: Backed by his father at last and now running the newly seized Zion's Landing resort.

characters.name: Judy Gemstone
characters.line: Married to BJ; still stuck between her father and a real role in the ministry.

characters.name: Kelvin Gemstone
characters.line: Reconciled with Eli and Keefe; now running a youth fitness program on the compound.

characters.name: Amber Gemstone
characters.line: Fully back with Jesse; shot a Cycle Ninja and became a congregation favorite for it.

characters.name: Gideon Gemstone
characters.line: Rehabilitated as the church videographer; ran the assassins off the road and saved his family.

characters.name: BJ
characters.line: Judy's newly baptized husband, now formally pulled into the Gemstone orbit.

characters.name: Baby Billy Freeman
characters.line: Reconciled with Tiffany and newly a father to their son, Baby Billy Jr.

characters.name: Tiffany Freeman
characters.line: Baby Billy's wife, just gave birth in a port-a-potty at the Zion's Landing groundbreaking.

characters.name: Martin Imari
characters.line: Eli's longtime fixer, now openly acting as the family's enforcer, wet work included.

beats.label: S3 · Power vacuum
beats.text: Eli begins stepping back, and the three siblings fight for control as ratings slip; Judy is quietly hiding a tour affair from her husband BJ.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the leadership scramble and Judy's ticking secret, both of which drive the season.

beats.label: S3 · May-May at the door
beats.text: Eli's estranged sister May-May reappears, begging him to rescue her sons Chuck and Karl from her husband Peter's doomsday prepper compound.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the Montgomery family, the season's antagonists, and the reason the Gemstones become targets.

beats.label: S3 · The nephews turn
beats.text: The Gemstones take Chuck and Karl in and even bond with them, but the boys are secretly funneling stolen fertilizer back to Peter to build a bomb.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants the bombing plotline while pretending to be a reconciliation arc.

beats.label: S3 · Naked lawn brawl
beats.text: Judy's guitarist Stephen exposes their affair. BJ confronts him and wins a brutal fight with a naked Stephen on the front lawn.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cracks Judy's marriage open and reshapes BJ from doormat to someone with an edge.

beats.label: S3 · Silo hostages
beats.text: Peter's militia snatches Jesse, Judy, and Kelvin from their homes and demands fifteen million from Eli, who refuses to pay.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The near-death that forces the siblings to see each other clearly and turns them against Eli.

beats.label: S3 · Monster-truck rescue
beats.text: May-May breaks the siblings out; when Peter corners them, Gideon crashes the Redeemer monster truck through the compound and drives everyone to safety.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Delivers the siblings' new pact to run the ministry together and their shared grudge against Eli.

beats.label: S3 · Locusts and a kiss
beats.text: Peter's truck bomb costs him only a leg. The Gemstones survive a locust swarm at their game-show finale, inherit Dusty Daniels' estate, and Kelvin openly kisses Keefe.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The end-state: siblings unified, Kelvin publicly out, family flush with new money.

cliffhanger.text: The siblings have finally agreed to run the ministry as equals, Kelvin has kissed Keefe in front of everyone, and Eli has stepped aside for good — leaving three untested leaders in charge of a huge church.
questions: Can Jesse, Judy, and Kelvin actually share power, or will one of them try to seize the whole thing?
What does Eli do with a life that no longer revolves around the ministry?
With the Lissons and the Montgomerys done, who becomes the next threat to the family?

characters.name: Eli Gemstone
characters.line: Has fully stepped back from the ministry, watching from home while his children stumble through leadership.

characters.name: Jesse Gemstone
characters.line: Sharing power for the first time, still the eldest, still hungry for the head chair.

characters.name: Judy Gemstone
characters.line: Just confessed her affair; she and BJ are working through it, marriage bruised but intact.

characters.name: Kelvin Gemstone
characters.line: Publicly kissed Keefe in front of the family; his religious closet is now open.

characters.name: Keefe Chambers
characters.line: Living with Kelvin, publicly acknowledged as his partner for the first time.

characters.name: BJ
characters.line: Won a naked brawl with Judy's lover; a harder, angrier version of himself now.

characters.name: Amber Gemstone
characters.line: Runs her own women's group at the church; increasingly the steadier half of her marriage to Jesse.

characters.name: Baby Billy Freeman
characters.line: Now a resident performer at Zion's Landing, still chasing a TV game-show career.

characters.name: Gideon Gemstone
characters.line: Working as Eli's driver; the family's most competent hand in a real crisis.

beats.label: S4 · The founding con
beats.text: In an 1862 flashback, Elijah Gemstone murders a chaplain, steals his identity and gold-plated Bible, and founds the family as a con man in a cassock.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Recasts the whole family as descended from a con; grounds the season's fake-preacher theme.

beats.label: S4 · Eli meets Lori
beats.text: Eli has retired to a Florida yacht; the kids drag him back for the annual telethon, where he meets Aimee-Leigh's old singing partner Lori Milsap and starts a romance.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's love interest and the emotional wedge she drives between Eli and his kids.

beats.label: S4 · Lori's dead exes
beats.text: The siblings distrust Lori and dig up her past, finding a string of vanished or dead ex-boyfriends; Eli waves the warnings off.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the season's mystery about who is really killing Lori's suitors.

beats.label: S4 · Cobb the intruder
beats.text: A 2002 flashback reveals the masked man who terrorized young Kelvin and stole the family's golden Bible was Lori's estranged husband, alligator-farmer Cobb Milsap.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ties Lori's family directly to a long-buried Gemstone trauma and names the obvious villain — before the real one lands.

beats.label: S4 · Kelvin comes out
beats.text: Kelvin wins Top Christ Following Man of the Year by publicly coming out on stage; rival Vance Simkins melts down on live TV and blames Kelvin for the loss.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kelvin's public arc completes and the family's most obvious rival humiliates himself.

beats.label: S4 · Cobb fed to the gators
beats.text: Cobb tranquilizes Eli and Baby Billy and cages them in a bunker; Lori's son Corey tracks his father down, stabs him, and feeds him to the alligators.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the obvious villain and casts Corey as a hero, which the finale then inverts.

beats.label: S4 · Corey turns
beats.text: At the lake house, Corey confesses to helping kill Lori's exes and shoots the three siblings; Dr. Watson the monkey fetches a gun and they kill him. Kelvin then marries Keefe.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Delivers the season's real twist, the wedding, and the family's exit position.

cliffhanger.text: The family survives one more attack together: Kelvin and Keefe are married, and Eli sails off with Lori, leaving the church fully in his children's hands.
questions: Can the three siblings actually hold the ministry together with Eli permanently gone?
What does a publicly married Kelvin mean for the family's standing in the evangelical world?
With Vance Simkins humiliated and Corey dead, who becomes the family's next rival?

characters.name: Eli Gemstone
characters.line: Fully retired on his yacht in Florida, now paired with Lori and out of the church for good.

characters.name: Jesse Gemstone
characters.line: Quit the Cape and Pistol Society after sparing Vance in a duel; still the ambitious eldest jockeying for the top spot.

characters.name: Judy Gemstone
characters.line: Kept her marriage intact and adopted the service monkey Dr. Watson; still the wildest of the three.

characters.name: Kelvin Gemstone
characters.line: Newly out award winner, now married to Keefe, the moral heart of the sibling trio.

characters.name: Keefe Chambers
characters.line: Kelvin's husband, formally part of the family after their wedding.

characters.name: BJ
characters.line: Walked again after his pole-dance injury, grew attached to Dr. Watson, and remains Judy's stabilizing presence.

characters.name: Baby Billy Freeman
characters.line: Made his passion project Teenjus with the family's money; briefly kidnapped alongside Eli by Cobb.

characters.name: Lori Milsap
characters.line: Eli's new partner, an old friend of Aimee-Leigh's; her son Corey nearly murdered his children.

characters.name: Amber Gemstone
characters.line: Still Jesse's steady, co-leading their side of the ministry alongside her women's group.
